headline: Waste reduction means not creating trash in the first place—the most effective form of waste management
universal_truth: Prevention beats cure; avoiding problems is better than solving them; the best cleanup is not creating the mess
fun_facts: The average American generates about 4.5 pounds of trash per day—1,600 pounds per year
Reducing waste saves more resources than recycling—prevention beats processing
Package-free stores are growing worldwide—proving products don't need excessive packaging
discussion_questions: What 'waste' do you create that could be prevented entirely?
Where are you solving problems you could avoid creating?
How do you design waste out of your systems?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Recycling is good, but not creating waste is better. The most effective trash management is never generating the trash. Prevention beats processing—the cleanest garbage is the garbage that never existed.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: We focus on recycling and disposal, but reduction is more powerful. Why do we overlook prevention?

options.text: Cleanup is visible, prevention is invisible—we notice problems solved, not problems prevented; but avoiding a mess is always better than cleaning it up
options.response: Yes. Recycling programs get publicity. Not buying unnecessary things goes unnoticed. But prevention saves more resources than any processing. The best solution often happens before the problem.
Recycling handles existing waste, but reduction prevents it—which uses less energy and resources...

q1.title: Hierarchy of Solutions
q1.script: Reduce, reuse, recycle—in that order. Reduction prevents waste. Reuse extends life. Recycling processes what remains. Start with the most effective strategy, not the easiest.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Hierarchy of Solutions"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Design Out Waste
q2.script: Smart design eliminates waste before it's created. Products designed for longevity, packaging designed to minimize, processes designed for efficiency. Prevention is a design choice.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Personal Prevention
q3.script: You create waste too—wasted time, wasted effort, wasted money. Before figuring out how to handle waste, ask how to not create it. Prevention beats cure in every domain.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Prevention beats cure. Avoiding problems is better than solving them. The best cleanup is not creating the mess.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 279. Tomorrow, we'll explore using things again—reuse. Until then, identify waste you could prevent entirely.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Prevention Check - What Waste Could You Avoid?
growTrack.learning_objective: Identify waste to prevent rather than manage
growTrack.activity: What 'waste' do you regularly create—in time, money, energy, things? Could any of it be prevented entirely? Before solving problems, ask if you could avoid creating them. Prevention is the first and best solution.
